content.text: {"obligations":{"reduction":{"status":"written_and_valid","quote":null,"witness":null,"load_bearing":null},"lower_bound":{"status":"written_but_invalid","quote":"Since $|E|<|V|$, the multigraph $G$ contains no cycle and no loop: a cycle or a loop through $v$ vertices already uses at least $v$ edges, so a graph containing one would have at least as many edges as vertices, forcing $|E|\\ge|V|$ — impossible.","witness":"Counterexample: take $n=2$, so the original geometric pieces are $1/7,2/7,4/7$. Split $4/7$ into $5/14,3/14$ and split $2/7$ into $11/70,9/70$. The sorted parts are $25/70,15/70,11/70,10/70,9/70$. Thus the first rank-pair consists of two parts from the $4/7$ piece and creates a loop at vertex 2; the second pair joins vertices 1 and 0. Hence $|E|=2<3=|V|$, yet $G$ has a loop. A cyclic component can coexist with other components, so the quoted inference is false.","load_bearing":"The proof next needs the component containing vertex $n$ to be a simple tree admitting a proper two-colouring. In this counterexample that very component has a loop, so the colouring and opposite-sign cancellation argument cannot be applied."},"upper_bound":{"status":"written_and_valid","quote":null,"witness":null,"load_bearing":null}},"S_valid":1,"wrong_answer_stated":false,"notes":"The closed-form answer, reduction, and upper construction are valid as written.
